mutations.after: // mutated: copy.timeline dropped from the hashed payload
mutations.because: hashCopy's payload must cover copy.timeline in full — every beat's text, weight and optional background, plus the timeline's own transition and keyBeat — not just campaignMessage/localizedMessage. Dropping the timeline spread means two briefs that differ only in a beat's text, weight, or background hash identically: the beat-text, beat-background and beat-weight tests in VariationPolicy.vo.test.ts ("hashCopy — the brief's copy surface, independent of hashPolicy") assert the two hashes differ, so all three fail once the timeline never reaches the hasher.

This is the Qodo-found gap this fix round closes: `weight` is a beat's share of the clip's duration (CopyTimeline.vo.ts:40-57) and changes what gets rendered, so it belongs in hashCopy's payload beside `text`/`background`. Dropping only the `weight` field from the mapped beat leaves `text` and `background` still covered (so those two tests are unaffected) but makes two briefs differing only in a beat's weight hash identically — the new "two briefs differing only in a beat's weight hash differently" test fails.
command: differing only in a beat's weight

mutations.after: // mutated: localizedMessage dropped from the hashed payload
mutations.because: localizedMessage is part of the copy surface §35 names and is meant to be in hashCopy's payload, but until this fix round no test constructed a brief carrying one — a CI coverage gap (VariationPolicy.vo.ts branches 99.22%, this ternary's true arm never taken) that traced back to the brief's own test list never naming the field. Dropping the conditional spread means two briefs differing only in localizedMessage hash identically, and a brief with one hashes the same as the same brief without it — both new tests ("two briefs differing only in localizedMessage hash differently" and "a brief with a localizedMessage hashes differently from the same brief without one") fail.

An absent expectedCopyHash means the persisted report predates this field and must take the no-pin path (§35's documented decision), the same way an absent expectedPolicyHash already does. Removing the `!== undefined` guard makes `planned.value.copyHash !== expectedCopyHash` compare a real hash string against `undefined`, which is always true — every re-roll of a pre-existing report is now wrongly refused. The pipeline.test.ts case that runs with expectedCopyHash left undefined ("runCampaign pins a re-roll to expectedCopyHash …", the noPin assertion) expects success and gets a refusal instead.
